Implementation-relevant•Official company announcement•February 3, 2026

Quanterix announced an FDA 510(k) submission for the five-analyte LucentAD Complete test

Quanterix reported submitting a Simoa-based p-tau217, Aβ42, Aβ40, GFAP, and NfL algorithm to FDA; this was a submission announcement, not a clearance or an independent validation report.

Key quantitative result: Five reported inputs: p-tau217, Aβ42, Aβ40, GFAP, and NfL.

Bloodp-tau217Aβ42Biological confirmation

Added September 4, 2026 · Quanterix release:2026-02-03

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The announcement moved a publicly available five-analyte LDT toward FDA review. The company reported three independent cohorts totaling more than 1,800 symptomatic participants. The release does not provide a decision summary, full contingency tables, or proof of clearance.

Study design

Manufacturer-reported regulatory package based on three independent cohorts with more than 1,800 symptomatic participants. Public patient-level methods and complete performance tables were not provided in the announcement.

Key quantitative results

  • Five reported inputs: p-tau217, Aβ42, Aβ40, GFAP, and NfL.
  • More than 1,800 symptomatic participants were reported across three independent cohorts.
  • No FDA decision, authorized intended use, public cutoff table, or independently peer-reviewed pivotal data accompanied the release.

What changed

A marketed CLIA LDT was publicly reported as entering FDA premarket review as a multi-analyte algorithmic assay.

Strength of evidence

Regulatory-process evidence only. The submission is verifiable as a company statement; clinical claims remain manufacturer-reported until the FDA record or full study is public.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

No clinical practice change follows from a submission alone. FDA review could later clarify intended population, thresholds, limitations, and performance.

Field medical relevance

Use this distinction when asked whether LucentAD Complete is FDA cleared: the test has been offered as an LDT, while the February event was an announced submission.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Directly relevant to Simoa and the transition from an ultrasensitive research platform to centralized clinical testing; it does not establish decentralized implementation.

Access or reimbursement relevance

A submission does not determine payer coverage, payment, or patient out-of-pocket cost.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Is LucentAD Complete FDA cleared?
No clearance was verified in the FDA database as of September 4, 2026. Quanterix announced a 510(k) submission.
Do five analytes prove better clinical performance?
No. The release does not provide an appropriate head-to-head comparison showing superiority over a single-marker strategy.
Can the test be ordered?
The company describes LucentAD Complete as a CLIA laboratory-developed test. Availability is distinct from FDA authorization and from coverage.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Manufacturer announcement
  • No public FDA decision summary
  • No full pivotal performance table
  • No independent verification of comparative claims
